facts.text: I asked for dialogue for the last two paragraphs of a story.
I said the dialogue should set up a slow revelation to David that the tommy in his past was his son.
I wanted the characters to continue walking and talking about shared experiences and struggles.
I wanted Tommy to feel closeness and connection with his dad that he never thought was possible.
I wanted Tommy to realize that even if their experiences are different, they both understand what it is like to feel alone and misunderstood.
I wanted the scene to include Tommy heading back home with his dad.
I wanted Tommy to feel newfound empathy and appreciation for his dad.
I wanted Tommy to acknowledge that they still have their own struggles to face but that they can face them together.
I said the previous draft had too much summary.
I requested actual facts and emotions in their conversation rather than words of encouragement and thanks.
I asked for the scene to be gritty, painful, and raw with emotion.
I asked for David to share painful stories that he does not have resolution on yet.
I asked for the writing to be really, really detailed.

keyphrases: tommy in his past was his son
